title: Bias-Aware Word BiLSTM Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution lowercases comments, splits words and punctuation, truncates to 220 tokens, and builds a training-only vocabulary of up to 200,000 tokens occurring at least twice; other tokens map to UNK. A randomly initialized 300-dimensional embedding with spatial dropout feeds two stacked bidirectional LSTMs. Masked mean and max sequence pooling are concatenated, passed through two residual ReLU linear layers, and used for a toxicity logit and identity-attribute auxiliary logits. Training uses length-bucketed, shuffled batches for four epochs. The main binary cross-entropy loss applies normalized bias-aware row weights that emphasize subgroup examples and toxic/non-toxic subgroup contrast cases. Auxiliary masked binary cross-entropy predicts available identity labels, added with weight 1. Adam uses learning rate 0.001, exponential 0.6 per-epoch decay, and gradient-norm clipping at 1. Validation inference batches by length and outputs sigmoid toxicity probabilities.
